title: Security posture discovery with Coastal Analytics
summary: Discovery focused on Coastal Analytics' security requirements for deploying Redwood. Key topics: SOC 2 / ISO certification expectations, SSO/SAML and IdP integration, RBAC and least privilege, audit logging & retention, encryption and KMS support, and options between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Customer asked for SOC2 artifacts, SAML setup guide, data residency notes, and an architecture diagram for private deployment. Next steps agreed: share security pack, schedule technical deep-dive/SE session to walk through network topology, and scope a 30-day pilot on Dedicated for evaluation.
topics: SOC 2 and ISO status and reports
SSO / SAML integration and IdP support
RBAC and role model for multi-tenant teams
Audit logs, log retention, and export
Encryption at rest / in transit and KMS/HSM integration
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pros/cons
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-27 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rosa (CSM), Jared (CIO), Priya (SecEng), Daniel (Head ML), Aisha (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you taking time. quick intros?
[00:08] Jared: Sure, Jared Morris, CIO at Coastal Analytics, we run ML infra and we're evaluating vendors for model serving and inference.
[00:15] Priya: Priya Singh, security engineer, I'll be driving the security checklist and controls.
[00:19] Daniel: Daniel Park, leads ML, interested in latency/cost tradeoffs and private deployment.
[00:24] Aisha: Aisha Khan, procurement, I'll handle contracting questions later.
[00:28] Maya: Great. Liam and I from Redwood, Liam will cover tech details.

[02:05] Liam: Thanks. quick agenda: go through security posture - SOC2/ISO, auth (SSO/SAML), RBAC, logging, encryption/KMS, data residency and retention, then talk deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private) and next steps. sound good?
[02:18] Jared: Yep.

[04:12] Priya: First question - are you SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified today? and can we get the report?
[04:25] Maya: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, we can share the attestation and the SOC 2 report under an NDA. we'll attach the current cycle report - it's last audited Q4 2025.
[04:38] Priya: Great, we'll need the details around scope - whether hosted API is included and what Dedicated/Private looks like in scope.
[04:47] Liam: Good call. Hosted API and Redwood control plane are in scope for SOC2. For Dedicated, depending on contract we can include dedicated pools under the scope; for Private (customer-managed control plane) the customer typically owns SOC scope for the on-prem components - we provide a deployable package and our security docs to support your internal audit.

[07:00] Daniel: On SSO - we use Okta and Azure AD, need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. how mature are your SSO integrations?
[07:12] Liam: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Okta and Azure AD are standard - we also have OIDC for some flows. we can share our SAML metadata and a step-by-step integration doc.
[07:30] Priya: How about session duration, reauth policies, and role mapping? we need to map IdP groups to RBAC roles.
[07:40] Liam: Yes, Redwood Console supports group-to-role mapping. you can map IdP groups to predefined roles (admin, developer, viewer) and create custom roles with fine-grained permissions. we also support session expiry and require MFA upstream at the IdP.

[09:55] Priya: Audit logging - we need tamper-evident logs and a way to export them to our SIEM (we use Splunk). retention needs to be at least 1 year, ideally 3 for some services.
[10:10] Liam: Audit logs are available for console/API activity and model inference events. logs can be streamed to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS or pushed to a customer S3 bucket. retention is configurable: hosted default is 90 days, enterprise add-on can be set to longer retention (1-3 years). for Dedicated, we can keep logs in your VPC and you control retention.
[10:38] Priya: Are logs signed or verifiable? we may require log integrity controls.
[10:45] Liam: We maintain append-only logs and provide signed exports for audit requests; for dedicated/private we can enable additional verification/integrity measures. i'll capture exact controls and include them in the security pack.

[13:00] Jared: Encryption, KMS - do you support customer-managed keys? HSM?
[13:08] Maya: Yes CMK support. for Hosted we integrate with cloud KMS (customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can enable envelope encryption. for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS or HSM and we integrate via standard APIs.
[13:30] Priya: What's the encryption at rest for model weights and cache (KV cache)?
[13:38] Liam: Model artifacts in our managed registry and KV cache are encrypted at rest. in hosted mode we control key wrapping unless you supply CMKs. For Dedicated/Private you can ensure keys are in your KMS.

[15:12] Daniel: Data retention: inference payloads - how long are prompts and outputs retained? we have PII concerns.
[15:22] Maya: By default, hosted API retains logs/requests for 30 days for debugging, and you can opt-out. we offer settings to not persist prompts for privacy-sensitive workloads. Dedicated/Private gives you full control, you can disable retention or route logs to your storage.
[15:44] Priya: Do you support field-level redaction or PII scrubbing?
[15:50] Liam: We have content-filtering hooks and can integrate pre-processing to redact PII client-side; we also have patterns customers use in their request pipelines. we can share guidance and a sample Lambda for redaction.

[18:05] Priya: Network controls - for Dedicated/Private we need VPC peering, private endpoints, and egress control. is that supported?
[18:15] Liam: Yes. Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. Private offers a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC. we also have options to restrict egress and pin regions for data residency. we'll include network topology diagrams.

[20:30] Jared: Liability and breach notification - what are your SLAs and incident response commitments?
[20:40] Maya: Standard enterprise contract includes SLA targets for availability on Dedicated, incident response timelines, and breach notification within contractual windows. we'll share our security incident response policy and runbooks under NDA.

[23:10] Aisha: From procurement perspective, what's the minimum term for Dedicated / Private? and do you support security addendum / DPA?
[23:22] Maya: Dedicated is typically a 12-month reserved capacity contract; Private is enterprise license with negotiated terms. we do provide DPA, security addendum, and can sign standard enterprise clauses.

[25:45] Daniel: For performance benchmarking - can we run a pilot to validate latency and model quality? we want a Dedicated pool to simulate production traffic.
[25:55] Liam: Absolutely. typical flow is a 30-day pilot on Dedicated with a scoped commit to provision a small GPU pool. we'll run benchmarks, capture latency percentiles, and provide tuning guidance (batching, KV caching, quantization profiles).

[28:10] Priya: A few nitty-gritty questions: do you support SOC 2 encryption key rotation policies, access logging for KMS, and role separation for key admins?
[28:22] Liam: Yes - we recommend customer rotate CMKs on a cadence; KMS access logging is supported via CloudTrail. we also support separation of duties; RBAC roles can restrict key management actions. we'll include the key rotation/management checklist.

[31:00] Priya: How do you handle secrets - e.g., model signing keys or service account creds?
[31:08] Liam: Secrets are stored in a secrets manager (encrypted at rest), access limited by RBAC, and rotated regularly. for Private deployments, secrets live in your vault.

[33:40] Jared: Any customers in regulated healthcare or finance using Hosted vs Dedicated?
[33:50] Maya: Yes, we have customers in healthcare on Dedicated and Private; finance customers often use Dedicated with strict VPC controls. We'll anonymize references and include case studies in the security pack.

[36:00] Priya: Compliance evidence: we need network diagrams, encryption architecture, SOC2 report, penetration test summaries, and a current vulnerability management policy.
[36:12] Maya: Noted - we'll bundle: SOC2 Type II report, ISO cert, pen test summary, network diagrams for Dedicated/Private, KMS integration guide, SAML/SCIM integration docs, and our vulnerability management policy.

[38:45] Daniel: On RBAC granularity - can you lock model access per-team and restrict who can run inference on particular model versions?
[38:57] Liam: Yes - RBAC supports model-level permissions and model version pinning. you can grant 'invoke' permission separately from 'deploy' or 'edit' and audit through logs.

[41:10] Priya: For auditability, do you capture which user invoked which model with what prompt id?
[41:18] Liam: We capture request metadata (user, API key or identity, model version, timestamp) and a request id. prompts are retained per retention policy but metadata is always logged - that can be ingested into your SIEM.

[44:00] Aisha: Timeline - we're aiming for vendor selection by mid-May and pilot to start early June if possible.
[44:12] Maya: Sounds doable. we'll prioritize the security materials this week so you can review before procurement.

[46:30] Maya: Quick recap and next steps verbally: we'll share the security pack (SOC2, ISO, pen test summary), SAML/SCIM docs, network topology for Dedicated/Private, and pricing for a 30-day Dedicated pilot. schedule a technical deep-dive with Liam and Priya to walk the VPC setup.

[47:05] Priya: Also please include log export samples to Splunk and any signed log/export process docs.
[47:12] Liam: Will do - include a Splunk ingestion example and signed export process.

[48:55] Aisha: Contract questions - we'll need standard DPA and we'd like to review liability caps; we'll send redlines.
[49:05] Maya: Understood; legal will coordinate.

[50:30] Jared: Any blockers we should know about? encryption or retention that would prevent Hosted evaluation?
[50:38] Liam: Hosted is viable if you accept CMK integration and opt-out of retention for sensitive workloads; if you need everything inside your VPC, Private is recommended. Dedicated balances control and operational simplicity.

[52:10] Daniel: ok that helps.

[52:45] Maya: i'll follow up with the security materials by EOD tomorrow and propose times for the technical deep-dive for next week. thanks everyone.
[52:55] Jared: thanks, bye.
